newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures firm again late, most end up.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures firm again late, most end up.

text.p: IMM currency futures firmed again late and ended mostly higher.
Traders said futures firmed again late in mostly light trade, although activity picked up in yen late as June futures rallied to a fresh session peak during the final hour.
The move back up coincided with rumors that the Bank of Japan had followed through on its verbiage overnight and actually intervened to support the yen, floor brokers said.
"The BoJ was in at $0.008018, buying to $0.008043," said one weary futures floor broker who believed the rumors had substance.
Those futures levels roughly would correspond to 125.91 and 125.51, respectively, in spot dollar/yen.
In other pits, traders noted that one fund was active in the Australian/Canadian dollar spread, buying 1,000 June Aussie dollars and selling as many Canadian units.
Traders had differing interpretations of remarks by U.S. Treasury secretary Robert Rubin in a television interview.

Rubin said the United States shares Japan's concern on the yen's recent move due to the impact on Japan's external surplus. But he also said U.S. dollar policy is "absolutely unchanged" and that a strong dollar is in the U.S. interest.
"Everything he's saying so far is dollar-positive, but people are leery because of the verbal intervention" that they feared might materialize into actual central bank activity.

"Rubin was talking out of both sides of his mouth," said another floor broker. "But obviously, people are more concerned about possible BoJ intervention....I think it's (yen drop) going to be a creep not a leap."
"(Rubin) lost credibility in the market," said a third floor broker. "I tend to think that he's wishy-washy...his position seems to be wavering a little in what they're (U.S. officials) going to do."

Japan's finance minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said Thursday that Japan will deal decisively with excessive currency movements. Vice finance minister Tadashi Ogawa said recent yen moves have been excessive and that Japan will take appropriate measures in a timely manner. Eisuke Sakakibara, senior Ministry of Finance official, said recent dollar/yen movements were not in-line with economic fundamentals.

June yen up $0.000064 to $0.008025, marks rose $0.0023 to $0.5845, Swiss franc gained $0.0048 to $0.6854, sterling rose $0.0048 to 1.6222, Can dollar lost $0.0018 to $0.7206, Aussie dollar up $0.0002 at $0.7834, Mex peso lost $0.000200 to $0.122625.
